'''Ritu Karidhal Srivastava ''' is an Indian [[scientist]] and aerospace engineer working in the [[Indian Space Research Organisation]] (ISRO). She was a Deputy Operations Director to India's Mars orbital mission, [[Mars Orbiter Mission|Mangalyaan]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/aurangabad/MOM-has-completed-a-revolution-around-Mars-ISRO-scientist-says/articleshow/55641825.cms|title=MOM has completed a revolution around Mars, ISRO scientist says - Times of India|work=The Times of India|access-date=4 March 2017}}</ref> Giving tribute to her excellence in Mangalayaan mission, a Bollywood film [[Mission Mangal]] was created where Indian actress [[Vidya Balan]] did her role.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/science/science/260217/indias-rocket-women.html|title=India's rocket women|date=26 February 2017|work=Deccan Chronicle|access-date=4 March 2017|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://rocket-women.com/2016/04/indias-rocket-women-meet-the-women-of-isro/|title=India's Rocket Women: Meet The Women Of ISRO – Rocket Women|website=rocket-women.com|date=9 April 2016 |language=en-US|access-date=4 March 2017}}</ref>

== Early life and family ==
Karidhal was born in [[Lucknow]],<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=http://www.idiva.com/news-work-life/meet-ritu-karidhal-the-woman-behind-mangalyaan/15120277|title=Ritu Karidhal, the Woman Behind Mangalyaan, Tells the Most Passionate Story of India's Mars Mission|work=iDiva.com|access-date=4 March 2017}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://www.tedxgateway.com/portfolio/ritu-karidhal-2/|title=Ritu Karidhal - TEDxGateway {{!}} Independently Organized TED Event|work=TEDxGateway {{!}} Independently Organized TED Event|access-date=4 March 2017|language=en-US|archive-date=15 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170315213000/http://www.tedxgateway.com/portfolio/ritu-karidhal-2/|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Uttar Pradesh]]. She grew up in a middle-class family which placed great emphasis on [[education]].She studied in St. Anjani's Public School in Lucknow.<ref name=":3" /> She has two brothers and two sisters.<ref name=":3" /> Lack of resources and unavailability of coaching institutions and tuitions left her to rely only on her self motivation to succeed.<ref name=":3" />  As a child, she knew that her interest was in the [[Outline of space science|space sciences]]. Gazing at the night sky for hours and thinking about [[outer space]], she wondered about the [[moon]], as to how it changes its shape and size; studied the stars and wanted to know what lay behind the dark space.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.indiatimes.com/news/india/8-awesome-isro-scientists-who-happen-to-be-women-271697.html|title=8 Awesome ISRO Scientists Who Happen To Be Women|work=indiatimes.com|access-date=4 March 2017|language=en}}</ref> In her teens, she started collecting newspaper cuttings about any space-related activity and kept track of the activities of [[Indian Space Research Organisation|ISRO]] and [[NASA]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.vogue.in/content/the-women-of-isro/|title=The women of ISRO|website=VOGUE India|language=en-US|access-date=4 March 2017|archive-date=13 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170313202831/http://www.vogue.in/content/the-women-of-isro/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Karidhal completed her B. Sc. in [[Physics]] from [[University of Lucknow]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=http://www.femina.in/achievers/people/ritu-karidhal-in-indias-leading-space-programme-7128.html|title=ISRO scientist Ritu Karidhal's Mars Mission|work=femina.in|access-date=4 March 2017}}</ref> She Completed her [[Master of Science|M. Sc]]. in [[Physics]] from [[University of Lucknow]] and got enrolled in a [[Doctor of Philosophy|doctorate]] course in the Physics Department. She later taught in the same department. She was a research scholar at [[University of Lucknow|Lucknow University]] for six months. She joined [[Indian Institute of Science|IISc]], Bangalore, to pursue masters in [[aerospace engineering]].<ref>{{Cite news|agency=Press Trust of India|date=2019-07-26|title=University of Lucknow to honour Chandrayaan-2 director Ritu Karidhal|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/university-of-lucknow-to-honour-chandrayaan-2-director-ritu-karidhal-119072601322_1.html|access-date=2020-06-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Lucknow University Recommends Chandrayaan-2 Director Ritu Karidhal's Name for Highest Honour|url=https://www.news18.com/news/india/lucknow-university-recommends-chandrayaan-2-director-ritu-karidhals-name-for-highest-honour-2248097.html|website=www.news18.com|date=27 July 2019 |access-date=2020-06-01}}</ref>

She has been conferred [[Honorary degree|honoris causa]] (an honorary doctorate) [[Doctor of Science|D.Sc]] by [[University of Lucknow|Lucknow University]] during annual convocation 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ISRO scientist conferred Honoris Causa by Lucknow University|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/isro-scientist-conferred-honoris-causa-by-lucknow-university/story-bKd7YVqD1sGDNeFethKLCJ.html|date=2019-10-15|website=Hindustan Times|language=en|access-date=2020-06-01}}</ref>

== Career ==
Ritu Karidhal has worked for ISRO since 1997.<ref name=":3" /> She played a key role in the development of India's [[Mars Orbiter Mission]], [[Mars Orbiter Mission|Mangalyaan]], dealing with the detailing and the execution of the craft's onward autonomy system.<ref name=":1" /> She was also the Deputy Operations Director of this mission.<ref name=":0" />

[[Mars Orbiter Mission|Mangalyan]] was one of the greatest achievements of [[Indian Space Research Organisation|ISRO]].<ref name=":3" /> It made India the fourth country in the world to reach Mars.<ref name=":3" /> It was done in 18 months time and at a far lesser cost to the taxpayers - ₹450 crores only.<ref name=":3" /> Her job was to conceptualize and execute the craft's onward autonomy system, which operated the satellite's functions independently in space and responded appropriately to malfunctions.<ref name=":3" />

She supervised the [[Chandrayaan-2|Chandrayaan 2]] mission as the mission director.<ref>{{cite web |title=Who is Chandrayaan 2's mission director Ritu Karidhal? |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/technology-science/article/who-is-chandrayaan-2s-mission-director-ritu-karidhal/484323 |website=Timesnownews.com |date=7 September 2019 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=From Lucknow to the moon: How Ritu Karidhal took on the Chandrayaan-2 challenge |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/nation/2019/jul/13/from-lucknow-to-the-moon-how-ritu-karidhal-took-on-the-chandrayaan-2-challenge-2003457.html |website=The New Indian Express}}</ref>

When the United Kingdom assumed presidency of the [[47th G7 summit|G7]] in 2021, Karidhal was appointed by the country's [[Minister for Women and Equalities]] [[Liz Truss]] to a newly formed Gender Equality Advisory Council (GEAC) chaired by [[Sarah Sands]].<ref>[https://www.gov.uk/government/news/g7-gender-equality-advisory-council-membership-announced G7 Gender Equality Advisory Council membership announced] [[Government of the United Kingdom]], press release of April 9, 2021.</ref>

Again in 2023, India launched the [[Chandrayaan-3]] mission to land on the lunar South pole and finally [[India]] became the first country to soft land on the lunar South pole. Ritu Karidhal too worked for the same mission and led India to this huge success.

== Recognition ==
Karidhal received the [[UP Gaurav Samman]] award from Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on UP Day, 24 January 2024.

Karidhal received the [[Indian Space Research Organisation|ISRO]] Young Scientist Award in 2007 from [[A. P. J. Abdul Kalam]], the president of [[India]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wef.org.in/ritu-karidhal/|title=Ritu Karidhal|website=WEF|date=28 June 2018 |language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-16}}</ref>

Karidhal has also presented at TED and [[TEDx]] events describing the success of the [[Mars Orbiter Mission]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Citation|last=TEDx Talks|title=The Indian Mars Orbiter Mission Story {{!}} Ritu Karidhal {{!}} TEDxHyderabad|date=2016-06-28|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ySzBVayVhYg|access-date=2019-02-16}}</ref>

Karidhal was awarded an honorary doctorate by the Lucknow University, her alma mater. It was conferred by Governor Anandiben Patel.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edexlive.com/news/2019/oct/15/chandrayaan-2-director-ritu-karidhal-srivastava-gets-honorary-doctorate-from-alma-mater-lucknow-uni-8672.html|title=Chandrayaan-2 Director Ritu Karidhal Srivastava gets honorary doctorate from alma mater Lucknow Uni|website=The New Indian Express|access-date=2019-10-20}}</ref>
